source.name: Colorlib Bootstrap Templates, Tavola
source.rightsEvidence: The pinned repository includes an MIT license for its source. The Tavola CREDITS.txt identifies every included photograph as CC0 1.0 or Public Domain Mark. Both records and Bootstrap's MIT notice are retained in this dossier.

capture.method: Rendered from the pinned local repository with Playwright 1.63.0 and Chromium. No gallery screenshot or screenshot download was used.
capture.captureNotes: Lazy CC0 photographs were scrolled into view and decoded before capture. A closed off-canvas navigation dialog was hidden only in the capture page to prevent the Bootstrap 6 alpha dialog from inflating horizontal scroll width. No visible page content was modified. The measured document had no horizontal overflow at either viewport.

provenance.attribution: Colorlib Bootstrap Templates, MIT source license. Include the MIT copyright and permission notice with copies or substantial portions. The photography is CC0 or public domain as itemized in rights/CREDITS.txt.

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: A hospitality storefront treats the menu as its main content instead of a secondary card grid. A narrow operating-status strip and compact wordmark navigation lead into a full-width food/interior image with left-aligned editorial copy. The menu occupies a large ruled panel with tabs for service periods, course grouping, dotted price leaders, and short notes. A split kitchen story, asymmetrical room mosaic, booking form, and dense visit information close the decision journey. Source demo copy, business details, reviews, dates, and menu facts are fictional and must not be reused.

heroGeometry.mode: full-width atmospheric photograph with a left-aligned editorial promise
heroGeometry.alignment: constrained text column anchored to the left over a broad image field
heroGeometry.viewport: complete navigation, short promise, and booking/menu actions remain visible in the opening desktop viewport

navigationGeometry.mode: thin operating-status strip above compact wordmark navigation
navigationGeometry.placement: status is edge-to-edge; nav is centered in a restrained container
navigationGeometry.mobile: brand, a small set of utility controls, and a closed menu drawer

typography.display: system editorial serif for the main promise, section headings, and dish names
typography.body: neutral system sans-serif for descriptions, metadata, and form labels
typography.scale: large but restrained hero type, small uppercase rules, compact menu labels, clear price alignment

palette.ink: soft near-black with muted gray-green secondary text
palette.contrastIntent: light paper-like content surfaces over a dark status strip, with one warm action accent

imageTreatment.mode: wide hero photography, one split editorial kitchen image, then a room and dish mosaic
imageTreatment.crop: cover crop for the hero; irregular square and landscape crops in the mosaic
imageTreatment.focalPoint: keep the dining/food subject legible behind a soft text-safe gradient; use mosaic images as atmosphere, not as evidence of the client's venue

servicePresentation.pattern: service-period tabs followed by course headings and menu rows
servicePresentation.interaction: tabs switch the selected menu; each item uses name, aligned price, and one concise descriptive note
servicePresentation.adaptation: for a cafe or bakery, group verified offerings by real service or product category rather than copying the sample courses

ctaPlacement.primary: reservation or order inquiry appears in the hero and at the dedicated booking point
ctaPlacement.secondary: menu browsing is the adjacent lower-commitment action
ctaPlacement.early: the first viewport should offer the primary action without hiding the menu path

motion.primitive: native menu tabs and date/time controls with quiet state changes
motion.reducedMotion: all content remains visible and controls work without transition effects

mobileRecomposition.strategy: single-column menu-led page with readable price rows
rules: stack hero copy before the secondary menu action while preserving the image focal area
allow service tabs to wrap or scroll without hiding category labels
keep prices aligned and descriptions readable as menu rows stack
turn the mosaic into an intentional vertical sequence
stack booking fields and visit details without horizontal scrolling

prohibitedPatterns: copying Tavola, its sample name, menu, address, hours, menu prices, reviews, or chef identity
inventing restaurant history, awards, farm sourcing, wait times, delivery, or reservation availability
turning every menu item into a rounded card wall
using CC0 food imagery as if it depicts the client's real dishes or premises
placing a PDF or photo of a menu where an accessible HTML menu is required

requiredSignatureElements.description: a prominent, accessible service or menu board with category and item hierarchy
a concise factual operating or next-step strip, using verified hours only
an asymmetric set of client-owned or licensed venue/food imagery
a practical booking or inquiry close with verified visit details

acceptanceChecks: the first desktop viewport contains the full nav, a concise promise, and a useful action
category tabs expose accessible state and menu items remain readable without animation
all prices, hours, dietary claims, address, and reviews bind only to verified content tokens
desktop and mobile preserve the menu-board hierarchy without horizontal overflow
every visible image is client-provided or a subject-matched asset with recorded rights

review.scope: Pinned repository render, per-template CC0 image audit, paired viewport captures, and transferable menu-led composition only. Sample business claims are not approved content.
